newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan urges banks to seek loan defaulters trial.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan urges banks to seek loan defaulters trial.

text.p: The State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) on Monday ordered all the country's banks and development finance institutions to go to court against loan defaulters from September 15 to 30.

An SBP statement said complaints should be filed before courts against all such loan default cases for which an agreement was not made by September 5 under a one-time incentive scheme for the settlement of loans.
On July 5, the central bank had extended the deadline for loan defaulters to reach agreement with their creditors to September 5, saying there would be no further extension.

Recent banking reforms introduced by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government have given wide powers to high court judges and banking courts to recover loans currently estimated at 127 billion rupees ($3.13 billion).
High Court judges will be named to try cases for recovering loans amounting to 30 million rupees and above, the SBP said.
"A large number of lower banking courts are being set up by the federal government to try other cases," it said.
The SBP said action would be taken against those banks and financial institutions found not implementing its orders.
The central bank has been given exclusive regulatory authority over commercial and investment banks and development finance institutions.
